text:
The Predators went 8-2-0 in their last 10, including a seven-game winning streak capped by Roman Josi's shootout winner against Vegas, and suddenly a team people had written off is 12-6-5. The PDOcast and KSDK both asked the obvious question: streak or something real?

Our numbers lean streak, with a real goalie underneath it. Nashville has 49.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and only 47% at 5-on-5, but it has allowed about eight fewer goals than its chances against predict. Juuse Saros is a big part of that, enough for Yahoo to call him a Vezina frontrunner. Our standings model has the Predators about four points ahead of their play.

The lines tell the same story. The Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly line has been outscored 5-11 at 5-on-5 with 43% of the chances, and O'Reilly left practice early this week. The best group by results is Filip Forsberg with Nils Hoglander and Shane Wright (10-4), and Sports Illustrated wrote this month about how Forsberg broke out of his slump. The Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix pair gives up too much (43%).

Our playoff odds have Nashville at 62%. What we'd watch: O'Reilly's health and whether the 5-on-5 play improves before Saros cools off.
